q: Initial margin paid by a client for a futures position is:
o: Debited to a balance-sheet asset account ('Initial Margin – Equity Futures')
e: Initial margin is a current asset on the balance sheet, not a P&L item. It is released or adjusted on contract settlement.

q: Per the prudence principle in derivative accounting, on the balance-sheet date:
o: Both anticipated profits and losses are recognised
Anticipated losses are recognised; anticipated profits are ignored
e: Prudence rule: provide for anticipated loss (debit P&L); ignore anticipated profit (do not credit P&L) until realised. Asymmetric treatment by design.

q: Under Section 43(5)(d) of the Income-tax Act, an eligible derivatives transaction on a recognised stock exchange is treated as:
e: Section 43(5)(d) classifies derivative transactions as NON-speculative business income. Losses can be set off against any business income and carried forward 8 years.

q: Non-speculative business loss from derivatives can be carried forward for:
e: Non-speculative business losses (which derivative losses are) can be carried forward 8 years and set off against any business income. Speculative losses get only 4 years.

q: For tax-audit threshold purposes, 'turnover' from derivatives trading is calculated as:
o: Absolute sum of profit and loss per trade plus premium received on options written
e: Turnover = absolute |P/L| per trade + total premium received on options written. NOT the contract value. Mis-reporting this is a common audit trigger.

q: The buyer of an option pays STT only when:
e: Buyer's STT is 0.125% of settlement value, charged only when an option is exercised. The seller pays 0.10% on premium at the time of sale, regardless of exercise.
